messages:
ops-bot: ALERT: contbatch-path p99 latency spike detected in prod-usw2 (p99=1.9s, baseline 320ms). Auto-page to #eng-oncall :rotating_light:

sre-oncall: I’m on it. Pulling up dashboards (p95/p99, stream stalls).

maria: I’m the on-call. Seeing streaming stalls aligned with continuous-batching queue depth. p95 ~420ms, p99 ~1.9s across packer nodes. ETA to investigate 5m.

raj: Observed large mixed-seq influx ~10:13 UTC. Pack scheduler backlog jumped, a few packs hit max_batch_size and pinned KV cache.

anna: Any customer-facing errors? Support?

tim: No 5xxs yet. A couple of customers reported slow chat responses (latency), one support ticket flagged degraded streaming for a high-traffic org. Not yet escalated.

maria: Ok triage plan: 1) quick mitigation to reduce p99 (shed large batches), 2) gather traces & example request ids for root cause, 3) prepare postmortem if impact grows.

raj: Quick mitigation options: reduce max_batch_size to 16 on contbatch packers, enable preemptive-fairness (preempt_threshold=0.6) to avoid long waits for mixed sequences, and temporarily disable full-prefix merge (it’s causing oversized packs).

dmitri: Can we do a non-disruptive runtime toggle? We have a hot-config path: `/api/runtime/config/contbatch` supports live patch. Example payload: 
```json
{"max_batch_size":16, "preempt_threshold":0.6, "enable_prefix_merge":false}
```
I can push that to 10% of packers as a canary.

maria: Do the canary. Which pods? pick pool-usw2-rt1 first. Make sure logging correlation id included.

raj: Pushing to pool-usw2-rt1 now (canary=10%). Patch command: `curl -XPOST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://config-api.prod/contbatch -d @payload.json`

deploy-bot: deploy triggered by dmitri: runtime-config/contbatch -> pool-usw2-rt1 (10%).

(2m later)

raj: Canary is live on 4 nodes. Early telemetry: p99 on those nodes down from ~1.8s -> ~420ms. Other nodes still high.

maria: Good. Roll to 50% if stable for 5m. Notify support and start collecting request_ids for slow traces. Tim, can you collect example request ids from the ticket?

tim: Pulling logs now, will post request_ids in thread in 3m.

anna: Note: this is the same symptom we saw two months ago when a large multimodal customer sent many short prompts that packed with long-codegen sequences. Mixed sequence lengths amplify tail. Check `seqlen-mix` tag.

maria: Yes. Raj, also check KV cache churn on canary nodes. If eviction is triggering paging that could explain tail.

raj: KV eviction high on non-canary nodes. Canary nodes show reduced KV churn. Looks like large batches were evicting hot keys mid-request causing stalls.

maria: Roll to 50% now, watch p95/p99 and streaming stall metrics. Keep canary for 5m.

deploy-bot: rollout started -> runtime-config/contbatch -> pool-usw2-rt1 (50%).

(5m later)

raj: Rollout to 50% complete. Cluster-wide p99 dropped from 1.9s -> 980ms. Canary nodes at ~380ms p99. Non-canary nodes still at 1.7-2.0s.

maria: Good partial improvement. Next: plan broader mitigation while we investigate scheduler fairness problem. Options: global reduce `max_batch_size` to 16; enable stricter preemption globally; or selectively throttle noisy customers.

dmitri: Throttling noisy customers is heavier lift (billing/owner flow). Prefer global config change for now + follow-up throttling.

anna: Also consider temporary increase to `kv-cache-size` for packers to avoid eviction storms while we tune scheduling. That’s a quick flip if we have headroom on nodes.

raj: Memory headroom is tight on some pods. We can bump kv-cache-size by 10% on nodes with >20% free mem. I can script that and do a rolling patch.

maria: Do two things in parallel: 1) roll global config to reduce batch_size=16 and preempt_threshold=0.6 (gradual 10% increments), 2) schedule KV cache bump where safe. Raj, start 10% incremental rollout, monitor for 5m between steps.

raj: Kicking off global incremental rollout. Patch sequence: 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%. Script logs will post.

ops-bot: NOTE: PagerDuty page still active for severity=high until p99 < 700ms for 10m window.

(10m)

raj: Reached 50% global. Cluster p99 now 610ms. Several streaming stalls cleared. Non-canary nodes still improving.

maria: Keep going to 100%. If anything regresses revert to previous config. Dmitri, prepare rollback snippet: `{"max_batch_size":64, "preempt_threshold":0.85, "enable_prefix_merge":true}`.

dmitri: Rollout to 100% done. Observed cluster p99 420-520ms depending on region. Good.

tim: Support: notified customers in ticket. No customer-facing outage; slowed responses only. We updated the high-traffic org with temporary mitigation they can expect improved latency.

anna: Assign follow-ups: 1) root cause investigation to runtime (raj + dmitri), 2) postmortem if any customer impact escalates (maria), 3) longer-term fix: smarter batch packing policy that accounts for seqlen distribution (product/eng).

maria: Agreed. Immediate post-incident tasks: collect traces for top 50 p99 requests, annotate with `seqlen` and `pack_size`, and produce SLO impact table (customer list, minutes degraded). Raj — can you pull traces/sampling?

raj: On it. Will dump traces to /tmp/contbatch-traces/1752123456 and share a secure link.

(15m)

raj: Uploaded traces + quick analysis: 78% of p99 events had mixed sequences where short requests were batched with long ones; batch head requests waited >800ms while tail long runs consumed GPU. Preemption threshold too permissive for our current seqlen mix.

maria: Action items:
- Runtime: implement adaptive preemption that uses recent seqlen histogram per queue (owners: raj/dmitri)
- Platform: add automated detection and temporary throttling for noisy tenants (owner: anna)
- SRE: create dashboard alarm for KV eviction spikes correlated with p99 (owner: maria)
- Product: consider API hints for preferred batching (owner: product-eng)

maria: I’ll file the incident and assign owners. Since no major customer outage (no 5xxs), we’ll mark SEV level as sev-3 but keep monitoring 2h post-rollout. Any objections?

tim: +1. Support will keep ticket watchers updated.

anna: +1. I'll schedule a design session next week for adaptive packing.

maria: Thanks all. If metric regression occurs re-open channel and escalate. Closing active page in 30m if p99 remains <700ms. :white_check_mark:
